data.narrative:
Mach Industries, a Series B defense and security firm founded by Ethan Thornton, is evaluated against a comp universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms in the same sector and stage. The target has raised $185M to date.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-Progression analysis uses the $185M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $352M. Peer-Median analysis draws from 7 same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations spanning $300M to $3.0B; the median stands at $1.0B. Named peers include Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), Castelion ($1.0B), and Defense Unicorns ($1.0B).

The triangulated range is $299M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $676M. This wide spread reflects material dispersion within the peer set—a 10x gap between minimum and maximum—and the methodological tension between stage-progression (more conservative, $352M) and peer-median (less constrained, $1.0B) approaches. Key uncertainties include whether Mach's operating metrics and market position align with the higher-valued cohort (Dream Security, Harmattan AI) or the sub-$1B tier, and the relevance of public comps to private Series B risk profiles in this nascent sector.
